newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares end firmer in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares end firmer in quiet market.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares ended firmer in quiet trade on Friday but dealers said they expected the market to be more active next week following the closure of a public offer by the state-owned dairy, Dairibord's.
"The market was quiet because people were concentrating on the Dairibord issue but we should see trade picking up next week," one broker said.
The brokers they expected the Dairibord issue which closed at midday to be oversubscribed.

Meanwhile, the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's key industrial index rose 49.28 points to close at 10,387.80 on the back of tobacco company TSL 's 35-cent gain to 635, blue-chip hotel and supermarket conglomerate Delta 's 15-cent rise to 1,750 and pork processor Colcom 's 10-cent addition to 440.
Cable manufacturer BICAF was the day's only loser, shedding 10 cents to 310.
Dealers said the mining board was neglected on Friday except for reasonable trading in Wankie Colliery.
The mining index was static at 929.61.
